From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 21:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: priority availability uplift / bespoke p95 commitment for Lucentio

Team —

Quick summary: Lucentio (large healthcare analytics customer) is asking for a bespoke p95 availability commitment for their production inference endpoints as part of a purchase order we expect to sign next week. They want a written commitment of 99.9% monthly uptime (p95 response floor 200ms for short prompts; p95 token-gen latency ceiling tolerances for baseline model) with a two-hour emergency response SLA and an operational runbook.

They've pushed a contract deadline to May 5th and are leaning heavily on this availability promise as a condition for committed spend (expected ARR: $1.1M annual). They're requesting:
- a dedicated routing tier during business hours (M-F 8am-8pm PT)
- on-call escalation matrix and a prioritized capacity pool
- guaranteed fallback to a local-quantized model if the primary cluster exceeds latency thresholds

Attachments: lucentio_sla_request_v1.pdf (customer asks) and lucentio_operational_requirements.xlsx (detailed telemetry/region/ingress pattern).

As this is non-standard, I need:
1) A short technical assessment of feasibility + estimate of SRE effort to operationalize (Marcus).
2) A product/pricing view on whether we can offer a formalized 99.9% commitment with guardrails and what concessions (credits, higher commit) we should require (Aditya + Lauren).
3) Any legal/FT considerations we should flag early (I will loop Legal once we have tech/price).

Can you reply with the constraints and proposed path (canary, runbook, monitoring hooks) by EOD Monday 4/26? Customer call scheduled 4/27 10am PT.

Thanks —

Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2027 07:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: priority availability uplift / bespoke p95 commitment for Lucentio

Stephanie —

Thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. Quick read and initial callouts:
- Dedicated routing tier: feasible, but non-trivial. We can tag traffic from Lucentio and route to a reserved GPU pool; will need capacity reservation and a fast failover plan. Expect ~2-3 weeks of provisioning + automation work to make this production-grade (longer if we need dedicated physical machines).
- p95 200ms for short prompts: depends on model selection and sequence length distribution. For a 128-token prompt + 64 decode tokens on current prod models, 200ms p95 is aggressive unless we move to a trimmed, quantized variant (8-bit) and guarantee routing to low-concurrency nodes.
- Fallback: automatic fallback to a quantized local model is doable via existing routing policy, but we must codify semantics around deterministic output differences and failure-mode notification to the customer.

Operational ask: SRE effort to build reserved pool + alerting + runbook ~ 120 engineer-hours (SRE + infra automation) for an initial pilot; ongoing ops cost ~0.08 FTE-equivalent (monitoring/escrow). That's an initial ballpark — will need to validate with infra capacity team.

Proposed technical path for the customer call:
1) Offer a 99.5% committed uptime for the first 3 months of the pilot with a roadmap to 99.9% after we complete hardening (30-45 days).
2) Guarantee p95 floor by routing certain request classes to reserved low-concurrency nodes and providing an SLA-grade monitoring dashboard.
3) Provide documented functional differences for the fallback model and a compatibility verification window (2 weeks) pre-prod.

I'll coordinate with infra leads Monday for a firm capacity estimate.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Folks —

Thanks Marcus — those estimates align with product expectations. A couple of product-level constraints & recommendations:

Constraints:
- We cannot commit to 99.9% across the full global fabric without additional reserved capacity and a contractual commitment from the customer to a minimum monthly commit. Without that, the pledge materially increases risk.
- Any SLA that ties to latency thresholds must specify the request class (prompt length, model family, streaming vs non-streaming). We should not bake a single p95 number that spans arbitrary workloads.

Recommendations for the proposal:
1) Structure the SLA as a two-tier commitment:
   - Availability: 99.5% for the initial 90-day ramp; 99.9% thereafter contingent on a baseline commit (e.g., > $900k ARR and a 12-month reserved capacity add-on).
   - Latency: Commit to p95 ceilings per request class (e.g., short-text gen: 200ms; multi-turn chat: 350ms) when routed through the reserved low-concurrency pool.
2) Controls/guardrails:
   - Define a list of models covered by the SLA (pick from our Verified catalog, exclude experimental weights).
   - Include automatic notification windows and a Customer Verification period during which the fallback model is validated against acceptance prompts.
3) Credits / remediation: Offer service credits as the primary remediation rather than termination rights. Cap credits (e.g., up to 3 months fees) and require the customer to follow the runbook before claiming credits.

For pricing: recommend an uplift of 25–30% on top of the committed spend for the reserved routing tier + a one-time operational onboarding fee to cover SRE effort (we can be specific once Marcus gives firm hours).

I can draft the SLA language and the per-request-class latency table — Marcus, can you confirm the hour estimate and whether the 120 hours you quoted accounts for automation of the reserved pool and the dashboard?

Aditya
